name: Yamata no Orochi
description: An eight-headed, eight-tailed giant serpent of Japanese mythology, slain by the storm god Susanoo no Mikoto in the Hi River valley of Izumo Province. The creature's defeat yielded the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi sword, one of Japan's three Imperial Regalia, making the Orochi myth one of the most consequential narratives in Japanese culture.

aliases.name: 八岐大蛇
aliases.meaning: Eight-branching great serpent; the kanji rendering combining eight (八), branch/fork (岐), great (大), serpent (蛇)

aliases.name: 八俣遠呂知
aliases.meaning: Alternative archaic kanji rendering found in the Kojiki

aliases.name: Orochi
aliases.meaning: Great serpent; the short form used independently in later tradition

origin: The myth is geographically anchored to the Hi River (now the Hii River) in Izumo Province (modern Shimane Prefecture), western Honshu, Japan. The narrative is national in significance but locally specific in setting.
